label: Moved at no time: Over a supplied clock, with the prima via predicates taken at each time, f is…
term: moved at no time (never reduced from potency to act)
definition: Over a supplied clock, with the prima via predicates taken at each time (Moved t x r: x is being reduced from potency to act in respect r at t), f is moved at no time when Moved t f r fails for every time t and every respect r. It is stronger than being unmoved at one time (DEF-TIME-SLICED-FIRST-MOVER) and says nothing about whether f exists at every time or is eternal.
note: Analyst instantiation for #352 (option B), the antecedent shared by MoverMovedAtNoTimeIsInActOnlyReading and SliceFirstMoverMovedAtNoTimeBridge; its Lean body is ∀ t r, ¬ Moved t f r, over arbitrary supplied clock and respect sorts. UnmovedAtNoTime.at_time specializes it; chain_witness supplies a mover on the full integer clock that satisfies it, while feedback_separation reuses the existing feedback control to distinguish it from one-time absence. No impossibility of motion, existence at every time, pure act, or slice-to-all-time bridge is included. Claim AQUINAS-IN-METAPH-IX-L8-FIRST-MOVER-IN-ACT-ONLY-A reads In Metaph. IX, lect. 8 n. 11's 'primum movens' in this sense, as the agent at which a history of agents stops because it never goes from potency to act ('id enim, quod exit de potentia in actum, requirit actum praecedentem in agente'). That claim is the reading's source; the definition itself is not attributed.
